code_review.notes: NEW SKILL. Exceptional first-time code review performance. Complete understanding of dual purposes: quality gate (catching bugs before production) and learning opportunity (knowledge transfer between past/present/future-you). Mastery of GitHub review tools: line comments (specific code issues), review-level comments (overall architecture), three review actions (Approve, Request Changes, Comment). Textbook-perfect constructive feedback demonstrated in self-review exercise. Understanding of review focus areas: logic errors, edge cases, readability, documentation, performance, security. Professional response patterns: gratitude first, explain reasoning when context needed, implement changes efficiently.

constructive_feedback.notes: NEW SKILL. Masterclass-level tone transformation ability. Perfect example in Checkpoint 3: 'This code is a mess' → 'I am having trouble deciphering what is going on here. Have you considered async/await? Let me know what you think!' Understanding of psychological safety: appreciation first, collaborative language ('I feel like we should discuss'), specific observations, humble suggestions ('may be the better option'), invitation to discuss. Recognition that starting with gratitude calibrates expectations and reduces defensiveness.

github_pr_review_tools.notes: NEW SKILL. Complete mastery of GitHub PR review interface. Understanding of Files changed tab, line comment mechanics (hover, click +, leave comment), multi-line comment selection (click + shift-click), review-level comment button. Clear understanding of when to use each review action: Approve (thoroughly reviewed, no blocking issues, ready to merge), Request Changes (bugs, security issues, architectural problems that must be fixed), Comment (non-blocking suggestions, questions, compliments). Understanding of conversation resolution mechanics and re-request review workflow.

self_review.notes: NEW SKILL. Excellent self-review performance on own CatchBook PR. Successfully adopted reviewer mindset to find genuine issues (hotfix/* definition ambiguity). Three professional-quality line comments demonstrating all lesson principles: appreciation first ('It is great we are creating a branch'), collaborative language ('I feel like we should discuss'), specific observations ('what defines a critical issue exactly'), humble suggestions ('perhaps we can expand the explanation here'). Recognition that self-review catches 30-40% of bugs before others see them. Understanding that removing ego enables clearer evaluation of own work.

pr_iteration.notes: NEW SKILL. Complete understanding of PR update workflow: make changes locally → commit with clear message referencing review feedback → push to same branch as PR → comment in PR explaining what changed → re-request review from anyone who requested changes. Recognition that GitHub automatically adds commits to open PR when pushed to same branch. Understanding of commit message conventions for review feedback responses. Recognition that multiple review rounds are normal and healthy (shows thorough review).

psychological_safety.notes: NEW SKILL. Excellent understanding of psychological safety principles in code review. Recognition that review affects human beings ('even if the review hurt my feelings'). Understanding that positive tone reduces anxiety and defensiveness. Ability to shift from 'Your code is confusing' (attacking) to 'I am having trouble' (owning confusion). Recognition that complimenting good work makes critical feedback easier to receive. Understanding that tone matters even in self-review ('Ugh, this is terrible' vs 'Hmm, this could be clearer'). Demonstrated emotional intelligence throughout all checkpoint responses.

technical_communication.notes: NEW SKILL. Excellent ability to explain technical concepts clearly. Demonstrated in Checkpoint 5: Smallmouth vs Largemouth Bass domain knowledge explanation showing understanding that context may not be obvious to reviewers. Structure: acknowledge suggestion → provide domain context → connect to user value → invite discussion. Recognition that 'must fix' vs 'nice to have' distinction reduces anxiety and helps prioritization. Understanding of when to explain reasoning (tradeoffs, domain knowledge, unfamiliar territory) vs when to just implement (obvious improvements).
